summary: Reproduces the final text of the draft international standard for the ISO Connectionless-mode Network Protocol, a Network Layer protocol of the OSI model. It can run between end systems or in relay systems, and provides the connectionless network service defined in an addendum to ISO 8348. It replaces RFC 926.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 994 reproduces the final text of an ISO protocol for sending data across the OSI network layer. CLNP labels each data unit with addresses and control information, and can split a large unit to fit a subnetwork.

subtitle: The final text of ISO DIS 8473, which defines a connectionless network protocol for the OSI model.

tldr.problem: The OSI network service needs a protocol that can carry independent data units over interconnected subnetworks without first establishing a connection.
tldr.mechanism: CLNP adds a variable-length header with source and destination NSAP addresses, lifetime control, optional segmentation and options. It defines data and error-report protocol data units.
tldr.outcome: RFC 994 reproduces the final text of DIS 8473 and, according to the unit metadata, obsoletes RFC 926. Its status in the unit metadata is Unknown.

today: RFC 994 obsoletes RFC 926, according to the unit metadata. Its status in that metadata is Unknown, and the RFC reproduces the final text of DIS 8473.

sections.title: The Connectionless Network Protocol
sections.content:
RFC 994 reproduces the final text of DIS 8473, the Connectionless-mode Network Protocol (CLNP). The standard places CLNP at the OSI Network Layer and specifies its use between end systems, relay systems or both.

CLNP provides the connectionless-mode network service. It defines how network entities send data and control information, how protocol data units are encoded, and the requirements for implementations that claim conformance.
sections.plainLanguage: CLNP sends data units without setting up a connection first. This RFC is a copy of the final text of an ISO protocol standard for the OSI network layer.

sections.title: Services and Network Addresses
sections.content:
CLNP provides a uniform connectionless service over one or more underlying subnetworks. The underlying service can be connectionless itself or can be supplied through a convergence function over a connection-mode subnetwork. It must support a service data unit of at least 512 octets.

Source and destination addresses are OSI Network Service Access Point (NSAP) addresses, encoded as binary octet strings. The network service data unit has a maximum size of 64512 octets.
sections.plainLanguage: CLNP can use different underlying subnetworks while presenting one network service. Each subnetwork service unit must support at least 512 octets, and the network service unit can be up to 64512 octets.

sections.title: Lifetime, Segmentation and Reassembly
sections.content:
Each protocol data unit has a lifetime measured in 500-millisecond units. A network entity reduces the remaining lifetime as it processes the unit; a unit whose lifetime reaches zero is discarded.

If the unit is too large for the next underlying service, CLNP can divide it into derived units. The receiver uses the source and destination addresses and data unit identifier to reassemble them. Segmentation is not allowed if the originating entity cleared the Segmentation Permitted flag.
sections.plainLanguage: Each data unit has a lifetime, so a unit that has expired is discarded. When a subnetwork cannot carry the whole unit, CLNP can split it and reassemble it later if segmentation is permitted.

sections.title: The PDU Header
sections.content:
A protocol data unit contains a fixed header part, an address part, an optional segmentation part, optional options and the data. The fixed part is 9 octets. It includes the protocol identifier, header length, version, lifetime, flags, type code, segment length and checksum.

The address part holds the destination and source NSAP addresses. The segmentation part carries information needed to identify a data unit and place each segment when reassembling it. Options can request functions such as security, source routing, route recording, priority or quality-of-service handling.
sections.plainLanguage: The header identifies the protocol, sender, destination and data-unit length. Optional fields support segmentation and other functions such as source routing or error reporting.

sections.title: Discarding Data and Reporting Errors
sections.content:
CLNP discards a unit for reasons including an invalid header, a bad checksum, congestion, an unreachable destination, an expired lifetime or an unsupported option. If the original data unit requested error reporting, the network entity attempts to send an Error Report PDU to its source.

The report identifies the discarded unit, states a reason and includes at least its header. An Error Report is not generated for another discarded Error Report. The RFC cautions that receiving no report does not prove that a data unit arrived correctly.
sections.plainLanguage: If a data unit is discarded, CLNP can send its source a report describing the error. No report can also mean that the report itself was not delivered.
